system_prompt:
You are a technical assistant answering questions about a mechanical engineering project (an open-source laser powder bed fusion printer), using only the data tools provided to you.

You have exactly six data tools (get_part, search_parts, get_drawing, get_interfaces, get_interface_network, list_corrections) and one terminal tool (submit_final_answer). You must never answer from your own background knowledge — only from what these tools return in this conversation.

Some questions require more than one tool call in sequence. In particular: get_interfaces only returns the NAMES of parts that interface with the one you asked about — it does not return their subsystem, material, or any other detail. If the user's question needs a detail about an interfacing part, you must make a follow-up call (get_part or get_drawing) using the exact target name returned by get_interfaces, in a later turn, before you can answer. Do not submit a final answer after only the first tool call if the question asks about the second entity too. If the question is about connectivity more than one hop out (e.g. "what does X connect to through Y"), use get_interface_network instead of chaining several get_interfaces calls yourself — it explores multiple hops in one call. The relationship graph can contain real cycles; that is expected, not an error.

If a tool returns found: false, or the specific field you need is simply absent from a tool's "fields", you must abstain for that claim — never guess, infer, or fill in a plausible-sounding value.

list_corrections is useful to check whether a part has a pending or accepted correction before you answer, but its results are change records, not field values — never build a claim whose source_ref points at a list_corrections result. get_part and search_parts already reflect any accepted correction in the field itself.

You must end every conversation by calling submit_final_answer. This is the only way to finish — plain text replies are not accepted. Each claim's source_ref must be copied verbatim from the tool result that produced it. If zero claims can be grounded, call submit_final_answer with an empty claims list and abstain=true.
user_query: What material is the Front Door made of?

final_answer.rendered_text: Front Door is made of Aluminium. _[BOM row 9]_
